author: Inside Edition
description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed defeated Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic primary for U.S. Senate last week. Now, El-Sayed, a former public health official, is drawing the attention of President Trump. Trump raised eyebrows by posting side-by-side images of El-Sayed's wife, Dr. Sarah Jukaku, and Melania Trump on his Truth Social platform. El-Sayed faces Republican candidate Mike Rogers in November's general election.
title: Abdul El-Sayed Responds To Trump Posting Photo Comparing Their Families

author: Inside Edition
description: It's been exactly a decade since Kim Kardashian was a robbery victim in Paris. In 2016, Kardashian was robbed of nearly $10 million in jewelry by masked men who burst into her hotel room in France. Now, the reality star is again the alleged victim of a crime. According to the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department, a 27-year-old man has been arrested in connection with a burglary at Kardashian's Hidden Hills property in southern California.
title: Cops Arrest Suspect In Burglary At Kim Kardashian's Hidden Hills Estate

author: Inside Edition
description: Courtney Clenney is the OnlyFans model at the center of a sensational murder case. Clenney stabbed her boyfriend Christian Obumseli inside a Miami highrise in 2022, killing him. She claimed it was self-defense, but now she's in a Florida court, accepting a plea deal to a manslaughter charge, for which she was sentenced to six years in prison, with credit for time served. Many are calling a slap on the wrist for such a brutal crime.
title: OnlyFans Model Pleads Guilty To Manslaughter In Boyfriend's Death

author: Inside Edition
description: It's still the middle of summer, but when you go out shopping, be prepared to see lots of ghosts, goblins, 'haunted' decorations and, of course, candy. Why? It turns out there's already a big push among retailers for Halloween. Spooky season is big business; last year, Americans spent a record $13.1 billion on the holiday. Inside Edition's Alison Hall has more on the trend being called "Summerween."
title: What Is 'Summerween?'

author: Inside Edition
description: Thalles De Souza, 23, is headed to Yale University! After celebrating with family he realized he had to share the moment with some other people, his bosses at the Wendy's where he worked. De Souza says he started working at a Cape Cod restaurant in high school and shared his college aspirations with the higher-ups. He says he was surprised when they offered to pay his way through community college. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Wendy's Employee Headed To Yale After Bosses Funded His College Education

author: Inside Edition
description: As "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" dominates the box office, one lifelong web-slinging super-fan got a chance to recreate a childhood photo with his grandfather. Aaron and his grandpa Bernard took the same photo, decades later, of Spidey delivering a crushing blow to an adversary. It made for a heartwarming family moment.
title: Spider-Man Fan Gets A Web-Slinging Re-Do With His Grandfather

author: Inside Edition
description: Grab your cowboy boots! The hottest dance craze this summer is line dancing. Moving to music in a coordinated group is popular among country music fans, and that genre has experienced a boom in recent years. Social media has also ginned up young people's enthusiasm for line dancing choreography. To see what all of the fuss is about, Inside Edition's Alison Hall recently got in on the action.
title: Why Is Line Dancing This Summer's Hottest Dance Craze?

author: Inside Edition
description: Italy's Cultural Heritage Protection Unit recently released video of a remarkable underwater find. They say a shipwreck dating back to ancient Rome was discovered off the coast of Sicily. Footage shows hundreds of intact ceramic jars, known as amphorae. Amphorae were used to transport things like wine and olive oil. Italy's culture minister told reporters the 2,000-year-old find is “one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years."
title: Divers Find Ancient Roman Shipwreck With Hundreds Of Jars

author: Inside Edition
description: It's a tune we'll never hear the end of, really. A church in Germany features an organ playing the same song for the next 600 years. It's the slowest concert ever and a crowd recently gathered to hear the chord change. It's the 17th change since the song started 25 years ago. Its title is very appropriate: John Cage's "As Slow as Possible." The chord will change again in October of 2027. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: It Will Take 600 Years For A Church Organ To Finish Playing This Song

author: Inside Edition
description: Haley Peacock has to take time off from modeling the jewelry she makes while her hands heal.
title: Making Margaritas Gave This Woman 2nd-Degree Burns #shorts
